text.p: The Turkish Treasury's 399-day bond auction dominated markets along with a continuing liquidity shortage on Tuesday, bankers said.
Money and bond yields remained high due to cash demand.
The treasury sold 344.5 trillion lira of paper in the auction for which banks will pay 145.6 trillion lira on Wednesday, to be offset by 189.3 trillion lira of T-bill maturities.
In line with previous market expectations, the auction yield, excluding withholding tax, jumped 6.94 percent to 99.99 percent, compared to the previous 399-day bond auction on March 18.

Bankers had earlier said the Treasury would be forced to borrow from the market at higher rates to meet Wednesday's 189.3 trillion lira redemption after using all of this year's cash borrowing line it has with the central bank.

Overnight money mostly traded at 71-72 percent and brushed a low of 63 percent in the day before bouncing back at the close when the central bank funded banks with 700 billion lira at 72 percent overnight, 8.3 trillion lira at 67 percent via tomorrow/next and 15.2 trillion lira at 68 percent via tomorrow/week.
The average overnight money rate fell to 68.58 percent from 71.06 on Monday. The average overnight repo rate rose to 71.31 percent from previous 69.78.

Earlier, bond yields were mixed, rising on papers with 1998 maturities and easing on those having shorter maturities as the market awaited auction results. They firmed after the auction in trade with Wednesday value.
The most heavily traded paper was April 22, 1998 yielding 96.59 percent, up 1.32 percent from Monday and the yield on the second most active December 10, 1997 was almost unchanged at 93.58 percent.
After the auction results were announced, yields rose to 97.49 percent on April 22 1998 and to 93.85 percent on December 10, 1997.
But the April 29, 1998 paper sold in the auction at 99.99 percent yield, traded at 98.79 percent with tomorrow value.
The currency market was quiet as the lira weakened to 126,735 against the dollar from 126,670 on Monday. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
